summary: Unit tests written against a requirement can improve design, but tests of internal implementation details usually do harm; test real behaviour like installing all requested packages instead.
questions: Should I unit test internal implementation details?
What makes a good design-level unit test?

answer_card.title: Avoid testing implementation details
answer_card.answer_md: Test real behaviour, not internals. A test that checks packages are kept in a *list* confuses whoever later switches it to a dict. Instead test something valuable, such as that every package passed to the module gets installed. Clear names help, but leaving out internal-detail tests is often better.
